pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

2. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.

3. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.

4. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.

5. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language School.

6. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.

7. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

8. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

9. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.

10. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. Only a joining word

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

13. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. going

14. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

15. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

7. A — Where is the library?

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

10. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

11. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

12. D — run

13. C — went

15. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
